title: Frictionless Performance Canvas: multi-metric model & route dashboard prototype
creator: Mai Chen
description: Create a compact, frictionless canvas for per-model and per-route performance that surfaces latency, throughput, and token metrics in a single glance. This ticket contains the high-fidelity prototype, chart specifications for engineering, review notes, and rollout interaction patterns. The goal is to support fast diagnostics (p50/p95 regressions, token cost hotspots) while preserving low visual noise for product teams and SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows combined view for Model and Route with toggles to switch primary dimension (by model vs by route)
Latency view includes histogram + p50/p95 line overlays and drilldown to raw microtraces
Throughput view shows rps + rolling avg with selectable aggregation windows (1m/5m/1h)
Token metrics show token distribution per response, median prompt/completion split, and cost overlay per 1k tokens
Chart specs are unambiguous for frontend/infra: axes, aggregation, color tokens, and performance budgets
Accessible color palette, keyboard navigable time-range and series toggles
Prototype approved by PM and one backend eng reviewer for feasibility
chart_specs: Latency distribution (violin + box): data: per-request latency in ms; x-axis: route or model; y-axis: latency (log scale optional); overlays: p50 (solid), p95 (dashed); aggregation window: selectable (5m/1h/6h); sample cap: 10k requests per window; tooltip: exact percentiles, sample count, median anomaly flag.

Latency timeline (stacked microlatency bands): area chart decomposed by processing stage (enqueue, kernel, decode, network); y-axis: ms; stacked order fixed for visual stability; hover shows absolute time breakdown and link to microtrace id; intent: quickly surface stage regressions without leaving canvas.

Throughput (rps) + rolling avg: line + ribbon; primary series: instantaneous rps (1s granularity where available); secondary series: exponential rolling avg (configurable alpha); ribbons show expected SLA bounds; color: green->amber->red thresholds tied to SLA configuration.

Token flow minimap: stacked area showing prompt vs completion tokens per request over time; colors: prompt (blue), completion (purple); includes median token count marker and 95th percentile mark; supports per-model normalization (tokens/request) to compare different models.

Cost overlay: translucent band over timeline charts representing estimated $/1k tokens for the selected model variant and quantization; hover shows cost calc (tokens * unit-price) and alternate suggestions (e.g., lower quantization) with estimated savings.

Top offenders table: compact table showing top 10 routes by cost or latency increase; columns: route, model, delta_p95(%), tokens/req, estimated_monthly_cost; actions: open rollout, create incident, pin to dashboard.
Sparklines microcards: per-model/per-route microcards with three sparklines (latency p95, rps, tokens/req) and a colored state pill (ok/warning/critical); microcards link to full route view on click.

Event overlay and rollouts control: timeline annotations for deployments, canary windows, and policy changes; clicking annotation opens rollout panel that can simulate fallback and reroute options; requires structured events input from backend.

Comparison diff mode: small-multiples heatmap comparing two time-windows for p50/p95/throughput/token metrics; cells show percent change and are color-coded for direction/magnitude; supports exporting CSV of changed routes.

Responsive rules: on small widths (<900px) collapse microcards into vertical list, hide violin and show combined histogram; charts keep same data fidelity but reduce visual layers to preserve clarity.
Accessibility: all charts support aria labels, keyboard focus on series toggles, and high-contrast theme (alternate CSS tokens) per accessibility spec.
decisions: Use violin + p50/p95 lines for distribution to balance density and readability; feedback preferred violin over pure histogram for multi-route comparison (2025-02-12 design review)
Token cost overlay should be computed client-side from token counts + server-provided unit price to enable instant toggles between model variants without extra backend calls
Microtrace links will be deep links to tracing UI; tracing backend to provide stable trace IDs (engineering accepted feasibility, see ENG dependency below)
notes_and_feedback: 2025-02-12 - PM review (Lena Ortiz): prefer default timeline window to 24h for correlating with deploys; requested quick 'compare to baseline' button.
2025-02-13 - Backend review (Diego Morales): recommended limiting 1s resolution to 1h windows to avoid high cardinality; suggested server-side pre-aggregation endpoints for 1m/5m buckets.
2025-02-14 - Design review (Aaron Kim): asked to reduce microcard visual weight and increase tappable area for mobile; approved color mapping after accessibility contrast checks.
2025-02-16 - User testing (2 sessions): SRE liked the combined canvas for quick triage; PM asked for quick-action buttons on top offenders table (create incident, open runbook).
2025-02-17 - Security review note (Maya Singh): Ensure rollout simulator does not expose internal IPs; mask rollout metadata by default; confirmed with infra team.
open_questions: Should the cost overlay include reserved/dedicated capacity discounts (need pricing input from PM/account)?
How to best represent multi-model routes (routes that automatically switch model variants by policy)? Current approach: show primary model with a small badge; is that sufficient?
What is the retention window for raw per-request data vs aggregated buckets? Affects ability to show violin for older windows.
next_steps: Incorporate backend feedback: change default resolution rules and add pre-aggregation hooks (coord with ENG-8142)
Add quick-actions to top offenders table and prototype rollout confirm modal (security-approved wording)
Run a 5-person design validation session 2025-02-20 with SRE/product to validate microcard info density
Finalize handoff doc with chart spec CSV and example payloads for frontend (due 2025-02-21)
Mark Ready for Implementation once ENG dependency tickets have owners and timelines
